The <\/span>Baker Institute for Public Policy at Rice University<\/span> studied LEED as the most widely recognized and robust green building certification. They determined that green certifications are \u201cA tool policymakers can use to meet climate goals. But this tool is only useful if it is accurate, consistent, and effective\u2026 Research indicates that it is only effective to base incentives off Gold certification or higher, as these are proven to result in measurably lower energy use and carbon emissions<\/span>.\u201d <\/span>At redT, we <\/span>design and construct LiteHomes to the highest LEED standards and are now at the forefront of the sustainable transition of the building sector with LEED Zero.<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Net Zero - Achieving a Balance<\/b><\/h2>

A sustainable future in regards to climate <\/span>is one that balances the amount of greenhouse gasses (ghg) produced and removed from the atmosphere. As a major ghg emitter, the building industry offers a prime opportunity to level out our climate impact. Remember, almost 2\/3<\/span>rds<\/span> of Denver\u2019s ghg emissions are the direct impact of buildings, and i<\/span>t is predicted that by 2050, <\/span>40% of Denver\u2019s buildings will be \u201cnew.\u201d<\/span><\/a> Any path to reduce energy usage is admirable, but slight <\/span>increases in efficiency are counterbalanced by an increase in the total 'floor area' of newly built structures. This shows the <\/span>necessity of new development projects reaching net zero goals to be truly sustainable<\/span>.<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

<\/p>

\u00a0<\/h2>

Net zero energy is achieved when a building generates as much energy as it uses. <\/span>The source of electricity is a major factor in determining the amount of ghg emissions, and<\/span> electricity is quickly becoming a clean energy source as the production process is decarbonized. <\/span>The USGBC determined that buildings account for 39% of energy related carbon emissions; operations making up 28%, and materials and construction the remaining 11%. <\/span>The energy consumed during the long lifespan of buildings makes it important to address operational efficiency for the long term. If we are to achieve a sustainable future, we must rethink the way we design, build, and especially live in our homes.<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

redT\u2019s LEED Zero Certification<\/b><\/h2>

With the addition of LEED Zero, the USGBC now addresses a building\u2019s full sustainability life cycle, even after a house becomes a home. LEED Zero provides a path for operational efficiency by <\/span>recognizing buildings that have operated to net zero standards for 12 consecutive months<\/span>. Homeowner operations affect water usage, energy efficiency, waste disposal, and ongoing carbon output, and LEED Zero rewards those that are able to generate as many resources as they consume<\/span>. <\/span>Due to difficulties in measuring individual homeowner\u2019s habits, the USGBC currently only offers LEED Zero certifications for single family residential homes in energy and water. LEED Zero is granted as a complement to the standard LEED certification. For example, <\/span>our newest LiteHomes are being built to a LEED Platinum level with a LEED Zero recognition for net zero energy!<\/b><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Determining energy usage to receive a LEED Zero energy designation requires measuring the energy use balance over a year. The total site energy use of a building is the annual amount of energy consumed on-site, as reported on utility bills. On-site renewable energy is the number one source of clean energy according to the USGBC\u2019s hierarchy of renewable energy sources. On-site renewables reduce the amount of energy needed from the grid, having the effect of requiring less \u2018source energy.\u2019 Source energy considers site energy use as well as the energy lost during production, transmission, and delivery to the site. Because it is more comprehensive, source energy is the most accurate representation of a building\u2019s energy footprint and is the measurement that LEED Zero judges.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Energy Modeling<\/b><\/h3>

In order to measure our LiteHome\u2019s operational energy efficiency while still under construction, our Architecture team uses a system called building energy modeling (BEM) to calculate energy use intensity (EUI). BEM is a predictive modeling system used in new building design, and is used to calculate EUI, the energy use per square foot of a property. The Colorado Real Estate Journal described these measurements in an article titled <\/span>Let\u2019s Talk Net Zero: Preparing for Evolving Code<\/span><\/i><\/a>.<\/span><\/i> As the CREJ title suggests, this type of modeling will become standard practice as all new development in Denver must be net zero energy compliant by 2030.<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

<\/span><\/p>

Modeling allows developers to simulate the energy use of a building throughout an entire year of operation. This is necessary to build to code compliance, and more importantly, a crucial part of receiving green certifications for buildings that are\u00a0 net zero trailblazers. The most energy-intensive buildings are often larger, commercial properties because the floor area available is generally not spacious enough to offset the energy consumed. Understandably, residential construction will be the driving force on the <\/span>path to net-zero goals and the basis for sustainable market transformation.<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

Truly Sustainable Housing<\/b><\/h2>

Today, even residential buildings are generally not able to offset the amount of energy related carbon that they produce. Through sustainable construction materials and methods, and a design process that leads to long term efficiency, redT\u2019s LiteHomes are a leader in sustainable development. The voluntary shift we\u2019ve made to sustainable practices is a necessary transition to minimize the negative environmental impact of the built environment, as well as to lead by example in making the impact of healthy homes more visible. Our team accomplished a LEED Zero energy rating by touching on each part of a LiteHome\u2019s life cycle. Passive design elements reduce energy demand, energy efficient systems and appliances eliminate wasted energy, and renewable energy is generated for the remaining amount needed.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>

We believe there is a fundamental difference between development and growth that provides the opportunity to deliver sustainable housing. By developing homes that provide the same comforts while using less natural resources, we are not just adding extra space, we are making each home qualitatively better. In this way, wellbeing continues to improve with less consumption. Sustainable buildings encompass the overall ability to provide a comfortable and healthy internal environment without negatively impacting the external environment. Furthermore, while renewable energy, reusable water, and zero-waste systems deliver obvious environmental and health related outcomes, they also benefit homeowners with lower utility bills. Denver homebuyers now have the opportunity to buy an attainably priced home that aligns with a healthy and minimally impactful lifestyle.<\/span><\/p>

\u00a0<\/p>[caption id=\"attachment_16228\" align=\"aligncenter\" width=\"1920\"] Rendering of redT's LEED Zero LiteHomes[\/caption]

\u00a0<\/p>

LEED Positive Outlook<\/b><\/h2>

At the Greenbuild Conference in 2019, the USGBC announced that future LEED projects will leave a <\/span>positive<\/span> mark. Their vision, called LEED Positive, is that new construction will not only negate the impact had on the environment, but instead, be a catalyst in restoring environmental, health, and social challenges. <\/span>At this time, redT is focused on fulfilling our mission to Build A Greener Colorado by reducing our environmental impact to zero. LEED Zero provides a framework for our LiteHomes to transition from leadership in design to leadership in performance. This transition is underway with seven LiteHomes currently under construction that will be the first single family residential homes in Colorado to be certified LEED Zero!!\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

redT is building toward a net zero future today.\u00a0<\/span><\/p>

item.title: Simple Homes Partnership
item.dc:creator: tyler@redthomes.com
item.content:encoded:
We’re excited to announce a new partnership that will provide redT with an innovative housing solution within the green building space… redT Homes and Denver-based Simple Homes are now working together to Build A Greener Colorado! Simple Homes will provide our framing needs going forward. This is a huge win in our development process and for the development of homes in our community in general. As a “turnkey off-site framing provider,” Simple Homes specializes in optimizing the American home construction process by drawing on innovative European manufacturing standards. This partnership between two local and forward thinking companies will result in bringing more healthy homes to market in our community!

An Innovative Housing Solution

Building in a controlled factory setting increases efficiency in many ways, most notably by incorporating technology throughout the process. Considering the persistent shortage of skilled workers, simplifying the means of construction is more important than ever. Felipe Magallanes, Process Engineer at Simple Homes, described the need for innovation within the construction industry, “There is very little change to how we build houses now as we did decades ago. (Especially) compared to other sectors, via technology and automation that other manufacturers are implementing.” The adoption of digital manufacturing technology is long overdue in an industry that is supposed to be focused on development.

Policy

Factory built housing has long been a small percentage of the homes built in the US, but as we continue to see severe inventory shortages, innovative housing solutions are necessary. The Department of Energy realized this looming problem and has introduced public investment in companies with the potential to provide high quality homes on expedited timelines.  Simple Homes earned the ‘Advanced Building Construction with Energy-Efficient Technologies and Practices Award’ by the DOE’s Building Technologies Office in recognition of their modern production systems in an otherwise antiquated industry. A 2020 press release announced that “The research will leverage Simple Homes' existing and European-inspired panelized construction system and digital manufacturing platform.” Two years since receiving the award, these two innovations have advanced prefabricated construction to new heights!

Digital Thread

Simple Homes continually refines the building process by integrating the digital and physical worlds. The complex process used to frame a liveable space starts as a digital representation. Technology assists workers as the product is brought to life, and information is constantly gathered so that any defects or delays are addressed in future models. When Simple Homes was starting out, co-founder David Schultz explained to Denverite that “The factory will be equipped with European technology that includes computer-controlled saws and a laser system that projects blueprints onto the tables where workers assemble panels that will become homes.”  Their high tech saw, for example, is programmed to cut lumber to exact dimensions and includes software that monitors the factory’s supplies. In this way, the physical and digital world are not acting independently of each other, but instead building off of each other to create a better product. Using technology to monitor and fix problems that arise in production provides a closed loop feedback system referred to as a ‘digital thread.’

Off-site framing

Both redT and Simple Homes realized there must be a better way to build than the traditional methods. The negative effects that buildings have on the environment, and the overwhelming lack of inventory due to long construction timelines, are not cutting it. Fortunately, Simple Homes CEO and co-founder Jeff Hopfenbeck internalized Sweden’s long-term success using off-site construction and implemented this innovative housing method right here in Denver. The benefits touch every part of the build:
  1. Lower building costs
  2. Better quality control
  3. Faster and more reliable scheduling 
  4. Less material waste
  5. Safer working conditions
We asked Plant Manager Joey Manchego about the main advantage he sees in factory manufacturing compared to traditional, it was an easy answer. “The efficiency, right? We're able to produce a lot faster in a controlled environment than if you're on site… Here, we do it all in one step. and so it's all complete by the time it gets to site”

Panelized Construction

Simple Homes uses a panelized construction technique that is a facet of prefabricated building. Panelization is different from a modular build, which is completed largely in the factory before the structure is transported to the site. The controlled processes and digital modeling that are available in a factory setting assist carpenters in achieving high levels of precision and quality, and the benefits of a panelized method encompass each of the five points above without limiting design flexibility.

So how does the Simple Homes way of building actually work? Panelized components are cut to exact specifications by the semi automated saw. The cut pieces then go to the framing table where nearly every part of the framing process is completed, even adding windows. The panelized components are all shipped as a series of flat panels (vertical if windows are included) that are assembled on-site. A crane and a group of framers install the final attachments and seal the building envelope in as little as 4 hours!

Collaborative Design

The comment, “tout ce qui est simple est beau,” appeared on a recent post about one of our projects. The translation? “All that is simple is beautiful.” The benefits of simplifying design go beyond efficiency and resource optimization. A thoughtful design from the beginning creates beautiful homes as well. This is not to say that prefabrication is limited to modular design. In fact, the panelized technique is inherently meant to allow for creative building envelopes. 

Even though Simple Homes operates in the labor intensive construction industry, many employees are actually designers and engineers that aren’t working directly on the line. The in-house design team at Simple Homes specializes in off-site framing techniques. To ensure accuracy, minimize waste, and save time, a digitally fabricated model details exactly how components are to be panelized. The 3D model is referenced and adhered to through every stage of the framing process. This importance means that redT’s Architecture team will send completed structural plans to the Simple Homes design team to confirm alignment with the systems and technology available in a factory setting.

Building Innovative Housing

At redT, we’re committed to optimizing every aspect of development, and construction is obviously one of the most important areas to address. Simple Homes will help our projects to see improved quality, speed, and sustainability measures. We’re not only building better housing, we’re building innovative housing. 

LESS MATERIAL WASTED

Process Engineer Felipe described his role with Simple Homes as “My main responsibility is to map processes that we have in place, identify opportunities that we can get better at, and then implement those solutions.” Basically, using technology to consistently monitor and update controlled factory processes results in system improvements. This system of ‘process mapping’ is applied in many ways, one of which being material use optimization Once the design team comes up with a model, a ‘quantity takeoff’ (QTO) is created to estimate the materials needed for that project. There is a small amount of tolerance for waste built into the estimate, but at completion, any excess is added back to inventory and reevaluated. Previously mapped processes help to keep tabs on material that often needs to be ordered weeks ahead of a project, while also tracking the excess.  According to Felipe, the two main ways that Simple Homes is able to cut down on excess waste is by repurposing for future projects or by selling the material. Unfortunately, contractors working on traditional job sites will often throw away excess material that is in perfect condition because once a bid is accepted and the builder is paid, any excess isn’t considered lost revenue. Reimagining the way we build is leading to a change in how we think about the waste that construction generates. Simple Homes has reduced waste to about 1% of overall material used, compared to a level of 15% that is common at traditional sites. 

LESS TIME WASTED

Off-site framing is clearly an efficient way of reducing wasted material, but it’s also an efficient way of reducing wasted time. The panelized construction method reduces framing time up to 90% compared to traditional methods. Once on-site, the structural core of a recent Simple Homes project was weather-tight in just four hours! This is compared to weeks or even months that most builders take. 

Shorter production schedules also result in easier project planning. There is greater confidence in the costs and scheduling associated with what is generally a complex building process. In fact, Plant Manager Joey Manchego highlighted that even at a time when material and labor shortages are a major obstacle in the construction industry, Simple Homes is still 100% on time for deliveries. Joey described safety, quality, delivery, and cost as the primary measures that they grade themselves on (along with less waste, these add up to the five benefits of off-site framing mentioned earlier!). As redT and Simple Homes work together to meet the demand for more energy-efficient and attainably-priced LiteHomes, each of these operational goals are positively affected by a more efficient and timely production schedule.

Shaping the Future

redT Homes and Simple Homes are both dedicated to innovative housing in the US. Of course, our LiteHomes are built to the highest energy efficiency standards. Similarly, Simple Homes has experience building Zero Energy Ready Homes (ZERH), a performance standard that the Rocky Mountain Institute estimated only 1% of homes to meet in 2019. Our partnership with Simple Homes means we’ll be able to provide even more of the most energy efficient homes on the market!  A shift in how we build for the future is key to alleviating both inventory and environmental issues. Simple Homes offers a modern solution that supplies high performing homes through a simplified process. It is clear how our homes shape our lives, therefore, we are adopting a higher standard in how we construct our LiteHomes. At redT, our ability to build better, more energy efficient, and healthier homes is furthered by our partnership with Simple Homes. One more way we are Building A Greener Colorado. We can’t wait to get started.

item.title: The Health and Financial Benefits of Living in a USGBC LEED Zero Certified Home in Denver
item.dc:creator: tyler@redthomes.com
item.content:encoded:
Introduction

Living in a USGBC LEED Zero certified home in Denver offers a multitude of benefits for both your health and your finances. These net-zero homes represent the pinnacle of green building achievement, providing a healthier and more sustainable living environment. In this blog, we will explore some of the advantages of LEED certifications, focusing on how the certifications promote well-being, save money, and contribute to a greener future.

Promoting Health and Well-being

All LEED-certified homes prioritize occupant well-being, creating indoor spaces that are healthier and more satisfying to the senses. The higher the certification, the better the overall performance of the home (LEED, LEED Silver, LEED Gold, LEED Platinum, LEED Zero). Here are some key highlights: Improved Indoor Air Quality: LEED homes are designed to maximize indoor fresh air and minimize exposure to airborne VOCs (volatile organic compounds - toxins and pollutants), ensuring a healthier living environment. All of redT’s LiteHomes are designed and built to meet or exceed the USGBC’s requirements for LEED Gold certification. Our LiteHomes on E Mississippi Ave and S Dahlia St were designed to achieve LEED Platinum certification and will be eligible to pursue LEED Zero status. Enhanced Comfort:  Our LiteHomes are built with a focus on thermal comfort, providing a consistent and pleasant indoor temperature throughout the year. Window placement plays a role in maximizing comfort levels. Natural Light and Views: LEED-certified LiteHomes incorporate ample natural light and views of the surrounding environment, promoting a sense of well-being and connection to the neighborhood.

Financial Benefits

Living in a USGBC LEED Zero-certified home in Denver not only benefits your health but also your wallet. Here's how:  Energy Efficiency: LEED-certified homes are designed to be highly energy-efficient, resulting in lower utility bills and long-term cost savings. LEED Zero LiteHomes take it a step further by pursuing the highest designation and net-zero status. Our LiteHomes on E Mississippi boast solar power. Water Efficiency: These homes incorporate water-saving features, such as low-flow fixtures and efficient irrigation systems, reducing water consumption and lowering water bills. Tax Incentives: Many states and local governments offer tax incentives and rebates for LEED-certified homes, providing additional financial benefits to homeowners.

Environmental Impact

Choosing a USGBC LEED Zero certified home in Denver is a conscious decision to contribute to a greener future—and you know redT is all about Building A Greener Colorado. Here are some environmental benefits: Reduced Carbon Emissions: Our all-electric (no gas) LEED-certified homes have lower carbon emissions compared to conventional homes, helping to combat climate change. Some of the LEED certification points stem from proximity to public transportation and walkability scores further promoting lower carbon emissions. Choosing to live lite also lowers homeowners’ carbon footprint. Resource Conservation: These homes prioritize resource conservation through efficient use of materials, water, and energy, minimizing their environmental footprint. Sustainable Landscaping: LEED homes often feature sustainable landscaping practices, such as native plantings and rainwater harvesting, which support biodiversity and reduce water usage.

Conclusion

Living in a USGBC LEED Zero-certified home in Denver offers a range of benefits for both your health and your finances. These homes prioritize occupant well-being, save money through energy and water efficiency, and contribute to a greener future. By choosing a LEED-certified LiteHome, you are making a positive impact on your own life and the environment. Experience the advantages of sustainable lite living and enjoy a healthier, more sustainable litestyle in one of redT’s LEED Certified LiteHomes in Denver. Want to learn more about Mississippi LiteHomes? Explore

item.title: Denver's redT Homes: Pioneering Sustainable Living for New Home Buyers
item.dc:creator: tyler@redthomes.com
item.content:encoded:
Introduction

As the world becomes increasingly aware of the importance of sustainability, Denver's redT Homes is leading the way in green building practices for new construction residential homebuilding. With a focus on the homeowner's health and sustainable building practices, redT designs and builds all new construction to USGBC LEED Gold certification standards (or higher).

In this blog post, we will explore the benefits of choosing a redT LiteHome and how their commitment to sustainability sets them apart in the industry.

Sustainability and LEED Gold Standards

LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) is the nation's most recognized green building certification. All redT LiteHomes are designed to attain certification in the top two scoring categories of LEED (LEED Gold or LEED Platinum), ensuring that new construction from redT offers the pinnacle of comfort, sustainability, energy efficiency, and community.

Here are some environmental benefits:

Healthier Living Conditions:

Indoor air quality is a significant concern in modern homes, as indoor air can contain 2 to 5 times as many pollutants as outdoor air, leading to allergies, asthma, migraines, eye strain, and other respiratory illnesses. To build healthier homes for the Denver community, redT achieves Indoor airPLUS certification through the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. This certification ensures better indoor air quality and a healthier living environment for homeowners.

Energy Efficiency and Environmental Impact:

Sustainable homes, like LiteHomes, have a reduced environmental footprint due to their energy and water efficiency, as well as their proximity to public transportation and walkability. By incorporating green building practices and sustainable materials, redT makes every effort to minimize its environmental impact while providing homeowners with lower operating costs.

Increased Property Value:

Sustainable homes are not only better for the environment and the homeowner's health, but they also offer increased property value. As more homebuyers prioritize eco-friendly features, homes built to LEED Gold standards will likely be more attractive.

LiteHomes: Attainable and Sustainable Living

redT's LiteHomes are newly constructed, LEED Gold (or higher) single-family homes that are lite on your wallet and lite on the planet.

Designed in-house by redT’s architecture team, these right-sized homes provide an attainable price for homebuyers while meeting the demand for eco-friendly advancement in building and operational practices.

With over 400 LiteHomes in development, redT is addressing Denver's housing shortage and leading the industry in sustainable homebuilding.

Building a Greener Colorado

By choosing a redT LiteHome, new home buyers are investing in a healthier and more sustainable living environment and supporting a company committed to Building A Greener Colorado.

With a team of Certified Green Professionals and in-house experts, redT is the only full-service residential real estate development company in Colorado dedicated to achieving green certifications for all new construction projects.

In conclusion, Denver's redT Homes is a pioneer in sustainable residential homebuilding, offering new home buyers the opportunity to invest in a healthier, eco-friendly, and energy-efficient living environment. By choosing a redT home, you are making a wise investment and contributing to a greener future for Colorado and beyond.

Indoor air quality is a significant concern in modern homes, as indoor air can contain 2 to 5 times as many pollutants as outdoor air, leading to allergies, asthma, migraines, eye strain, and other respiratory illnesses. To build healthier homes for the Denver community, redT achieves Indoor airPLUS certification through the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. This certification ensures better indoor air quality and a healthier living environment for homeowners.<\/span><\/p>

Sustainable homes, like LiteHomes, have a reduced environmental footprint due to their energy and water efficiency, as well as their proximity to public transportation and walkability. By incorporating green building practices and sustainable materials, redT makes every effort to minimize its environmental impact while providing homeowners with lower operating costs.<\/span><\/p>

Increased Property Value:<\/span><\/strong><\/p>

item.title: Transforming Denver's Urban Landscape: Redefining Sustainability with Green Infill by redT Homes
item.dc:creator: aaron@smbadvisors.com
item.content:encoded:
As Denver, Colorado, continues to grow, sustainable development practices become paramount. In the heart of the future of urban living stands redT Homes, pioneering the use of Green Infill to not only redefine urban living but also contribute to preserving Denver’s distinctive environment. The commitment to sustainable and community-focused development by redT Homes is significant for the future of Green Infill in Denver.  

Green Infill in Denver: A redT Homes Perspective

[caption id="attachment_22786" align="alignnone" width="647"] Denver, Colorado, USA, downtown cityscape rooftop view at dusk.[/caption]

Definition of Green Infill in Denver:

In Denver, Green Infill takes on a unique significance. It’s about revitalizing and repurposing existing urban spaces to accommodate the city’s growing population while safeguarding the city’s integrity. redT Homes adopts Green Infill as a strategy to ensure that Denver’s development aligns with the city’s character, emphasizing sustainable practices that resonate with the local community.  

Purpose of Green Infill for redT Homes in Denver:

For redT Homes, the purpose of Green Infill extends beyond development—it’s about creating communities that thrive in harmony with Denver’s surroundings. By strategically selecting and transforming spaces within the city, redT Homes aims to offer residents not just homes but an elevated lifestyle rooted in sustainability, connection, and a deep appreciation for Denver’s unique atmosphere. [gallery size="medium" ids="22788,22789,22790"]

Benefits of redT Homes’ Green Infill Approach in Denver

[gallery size="medium" ids="22795,22792,22791"]

  1. Preserving Denver’s Charm:

redT Homes’ Green Infill strategy ensures that the city’s distinctive charm is preserved. The development approach is tailored to enhance, rather than overshadow, the local character and aesthetics.  

  1. Community-Centric Living:

Denver residents choosing redT Homes experience community-centric living. Green Infill developments focus on creating community around the accessibility features of urban living – sharing spaces that offer proximity to transportation, parks, and recreational areas that foster a sense of community among residents.  

  1. Environmental Stewardship:

redT Homes is committed to environmental stewardship in Denver. Green Infill minimizes the environmental impact of development, aligning with Denver’s ethos of embracing nature and sustainability.  

  1. Tailored Solutions for Denver:

The Green Infill projects by redT Homes are thoughtfully designed to meet the specific needs of Denver’s diverse communities. From energy-efficient homes to eco-friendly infrastructure, each project reflects a commitment to tailored, locally resonant solutions.   [caption id="attachment_20346" align="alignnone" width="632"] redT Homes - Commitment to Community[/caption] In the Mile-High City, redT Homes is not just building homes; they are crafting a sustainable legacy through Green Infill. By prioritizing the unique needs of Denver’s neighborhoods, redT Homes exemplifies how Green Infill can be a catalyst for positive urban transformation. Denver’s evolution is not only in its skyline but also in the mindful and sustainable way redT Homes is reshaping it for generations to come.   Be a part of Building A  Greener Colorado! Fill out the contact form below and start your path to healthier living. [gravityform id="1" title="true" description="true"]

item.title: CEO of redT Homes on The Strategy Behind Scaling a Company
item.dc:creator: aaron@smbadvisors.com
item.content:encoded:
Vincent Deorio, redT’s new CEO, reveals his strategies for the organic expansion of redT, advancing the mission of sustainable housing.

Ever wondered how a real estate entrepreneur transitions from distressed property investments to spearheading a pioneering green building initiative? Dive into “The Strategy Behind Scaling a Company with redT Homes New CEO Vincent Deorio” as we engage in a captivating conversation with Vincent, the CEO of redT Homes. Discover the intricacies of scaling a company and the visionary plans for sustainable growth. From his start in Southern California to overseeing expansive projects in 25+ states, Vincent shares insights into the challenges and successes of his journey. Uncover how redT, under Vincent’s leadership, is set to close 160 homes in 2024, initiate 275 new units, and acquire 350 more units of land in Colorado. This episode explores the dynamic realm of green building, company scaling, and the future of redT, providing a unique perspective on success in the real estate industry. (01:28) Vincent’s experience scaling real estate companies (12:10) Joining redT as the new CEO (22:50) Playbook for expanding into a new market

Who is redT Homes?

red T Homes is a mission-driven, values-based residential real estate development company in Denver, known for offering a comprehensive suite of services encompassing land acquisition, entitlement, design, architecture, construction, marketing, and sales. What sets them apart is their resolute commitment to “Building A Greener Colorado,” prioritizing the well-being of families and the environment. Their projects are built to a LEED Gold Certification standard or better, and they exclusively partner with developers, builders, and investors who share this commitment. As pioneers, red T is the first homebuilder west of the Mississippi to meet the rigorous US Green Building Council standards for LEED Zero Certification, resulting in the design, construction, and sale of healthy, eco-friendly new homes that combine beauty, functionality, and sustainability, making them a transformative force in the real estate industry.

item.content:encoded:
Dive into real estate development with Paul Ko, redT’s CIO, as he unveils the 2024 game plan and exclusive investment opportunities with redT’s incubator program!

Dive into the world of real estate development with Chris Lopez and Paul Ko, Chief Investment Officer at redT. In the wake of the 2008 financial crisis, Paul’s family development company faced bankruptcy, providing him with a crash course in the volatile nature of the real estate market. Fast forward to 2010, and we find Paul house hacking a fourplex property, a pivotal moment that ignited his passion for real estate investing. Paul shares insights into the evolving landscape of development, and redT’s strategic game plan for the upcoming wave of deals in 2024. Watch now to learn about redT’s incubator program and seize your chance to ride the wave of unique investment opportunities! (04:16) How Paul started developing properties (08:06) redT’s Incubator Program for Investors (14:10) Next 2008 crash – what are the opportunities? (23:50) redT deals: Limited Partner investing

red T Homes is a mission-driven, values-based residential real estate development company in Denver, known for offering a comprehensive suite of services encompassing land acquisition, entitlement, design, architecture, construction, marketing, and sales. What sets them apart is their resolute commitment to “Building A Greener Colorado,” prioritizing the well-being of families and the environment. Their projects are built to a LEED Gold Certification standard or better, and they exclusively partner with developers, builders, and investors who share this commitment. As pioneers, red T is the first homebuilder west of the Mississippi to meet the rigorous US Green Building Council standards for LEED Zero Certification, resulting in the design, construction, and sale of healthy, eco-friendly new homes that combine beauty, functionality, and sustainability, making them a transformative force in the real estate industry.

item.title: redT Homes LEEDing the Way in Sustainable Living: A Generous Step Towards Attainability
item.dc:creator: aaron@smbadvisors.com
item.content:encoded:
redT Homes LEEDing the Way in Sustainable Living: A Generous Step Towards Attainability

  In the pursuit of sustainable living, the cost can often be a barrier for many. However, redT Homes, a prominent figure in Denver's real estate scene, is breaking barriers by embracing generosity and belief in the benefits of their product. One significant move they've made is absorbing the LEED Zero Certification fee for new homeowners, a decision that reflects their commitment to both the city of Denver and the broader sustainable living community.  

The Value of Living in a LEED Zero Home

Living in a LEED Zero (the equivalent of net zero) home offers unparalleled benefits, both in terms of energy efficiency and overall health. However, these benefits come at a cost. The burden of the LEED Zero Certification fee would normally fall upon the new homeowner, adding to the already substantial investment made in pursuit of creating a more sustainable lifestyle. Recognizing this challenge, redT Homes has taken a proactive step to alleviate some of the financial strain associated with certification.  

redT's Commitment: Absorbing Certification Costs

redT Homes takes pride in their commitment to sustainability. They understand that building to LEED Zero standards requires additional investment, such as integrating solar panels, which can add between $15,000 to $25,000 per unit, and upwards. Despite these costs, redT Homes believes in the long-term benefits for homeowners and the environment.   By covering the initial LEED Zero Certification fee for new homeowners, redT Homes is not only demonstrating their generosity but also making sustainable living more accessible to a broader audience. This decision reflects their belief in the value of their product and its positive impact on the community.    

Investing in Long-Term Sustainability

LEED Zero certifications are valid for three years, during which certified projects must submit performance data annually. Renewal fees, which can be costly, underscore the ongoing commitment required to maintain these standards. By absorbing the initial certification fee, redT Homes is not only investing in the present but also in the future sustainability of their properties.  

Join Us in Embracing Sustainable Living

At redT Homes, we're committed to making sustainable living a reality for everyone. Sign up for our email updates to stay informed about our latest home sale offerings and join us in creating a more sustainable future for Denver and beyond.     By prioritizing generosity and investing in the long-term sustainability of their properties, redT Homes is setting a precedent for the real estate industry. Their decision to absorb the LEED Zero Certification fee not only benefits new homeowners but also reinforces their belief in the value of sustainable living. As we look to the future, redT Homes is on a mission to Build A Greener Colorado and a more sustainable world, one home at a time.

item.title: Breathing Easier: The Impact of Sustainable Homes on Indoor Air Quality
item.dc:creator: aaron@smbadvisors.com
item.content:encoded:
Breathing Easier: The Impact of Sustainable Homes on Indoor Air Quality

In the pursuit of a healthier lifestyle, many of us focus on nutrition and exercise while overlooking a critical aspect of our well-being: the quality of the air we breathe indoors. In Colorado, where environmental factors can significantly affect indoor air quality, sustainable living takes on added importance. There is a strong correlation between sustainable homes and personal health, and redT Homes, recently recognized with the 2023 Xcel Energy Sustainable New Housing Program Award for Best Individual Electric Only Builder Overall, has been at the forefront of responsible and sustainable living with each project, paving the way for cleaner, healthier living environments.

Understanding the Link Between Sustainable Living and Health

Sustainable living isn't just about reducing our carbon footprint; it's also about creating spaces that promote better health and well-being. Research conducted by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) indicates that indoor air pollution can be two to five times higher than outdoor air pollution levels. Poor indoor air quality has been linked to respiratory illnesses such as asthma and allergies, as well as symptoms like headaches, fatigue, and irritation of the eyes, nose, and throat. Additionally, studies have shown that exposure to indoor air pollutants can have long-term health effects, including an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and respiratory infections.

The Importance of Indoor Air Quality in Colorado

In Colorado, where residents often spend a significant amount of time indoors due to extreme weather conditions, the quality of indoor air becomes paramount. According to the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, indoor air pollution can be particularly problematic in areas with high levels of outdoor pollution, such as urban areas and regions near major highways. Additionally, Colorado's dry climate can exacerbate indoor air quality issues, as low humidity levels can lead to the accumulation of dust and other airborne particles. This can be especially problematic for individuals with respiratory conditions such as asthma and COPD.

redT Homes: Leading the Way in Clean Living

redT Homes understands the importance of indoor air quality in promoting healthier living environments. Through their commitment to sustainability and LEED certification standards, redT Homes integrates eco-friendly materials and advanced ventilation systems into their projects, ensuring that occupants breathe cleaner air day in and day out. Notably, redT Homes takes an additional step in promoting clean air by omitting the use of natural gas entirely. Studies indicate gas is a major contributor to poor indoor air quality and respiratory health issues. redT doesn't bring gas lines into their new developments, ensuring that their homes are truly clean and sustainable from the ground up.

Eco-Friendly Materials

redT Homes prioritizes the use of eco-friendly materials that emit minimal VOCs, reducing indoor air pollution and creating a healthier indoor environment. These materials include low-VOC paints, sustainable flooring options made from natural materials such as bamboo or cork, and formaldehyde-free insulation. By selecting materials that are free from harmful chemicals, redT Homes not only improves indoor air quality but also reduces the environmental impact of their projects.

Proper Ventilation Systems

In addition to using eco-friendly materials, redT Homes implements state-of-the-art ventilation systems that continuously circulate fresh air throughout the home while expelling pollutants and moisture. Proper ventilation is essential for maintaining indoor air quality, as it helps remove airborne contaminants and prevents the buildup of mold and mildew, which can exacerbate respiratory issues. redT Homes also employs energy-efficient HVAC systems that are appropriately sized to minimize energy waste and ensure optimal indoor comfort.

The Health Benefits of Sustainable Homes

By prioritizing indoor air quality through sustainable practices, redT Homes's projects offer numerous health benefits to occupants. Cleaner air reduces the risk of respiratory illnesses, allergies, and asthma attacks, promoting better respiratory health and overall well-being. Additionally, improved indoor air quality enhances cognitive function and productivity, creating a more comfortable and enjoyable living environment. Studies have shown that individuals living in green-certified homes report fewer sick days and higher overall satisfaction with their living environment compared to those in conventional homes.

As we strive to live healthier lifestyles, it's essential to consider the quality of the air we breathe indoors. Sustainable homes, like those developed by redT Homes, play a crucial role in promoting cleaner indoor air and better respiratory health. By integrating eco-friendly materials and advanced ventilation systems, redT Homes's projects set a new standard for clean living in Colorado and beyond. Investing in a sustainable home isn't just beneficial for the environment; it's also an investment in your health and well-being.

item.title: 10 Easy Ways to Improve Indoor Air Quality and Live Sustainably
item.dc:creator: aaron@smbadvisors.com
item.content:encoded:
10 Easy Ways to Improve Indoor Air Quality and Live Sustainably

Living sustainably goes beyond reducing your carbon footprint; it also encompasses creating a healthier indoor environment for you and your loved ones. Check out these simple yet effective tips to improve indoor air quality while embracing a sustainable lifestyle:

Opt for Natural Cleaning Products:

Swap chemical-laden cleaners for natural alternatives like vinegar, baking soda, and lemon juice. Not only are these options better for the environment, but they also help reduce indoor air pollution.

Bring in Houseplants:

Plants act as natural air purifiers by absorbing harmful pollutants and releasing oxygen. Consider adding spider plants, peace lilies, or snake plants to your home to enhance air quality.

Ventilate Your Home:

Proper ventilation is essential for maintaining good indoor air quality. Open windows regularly to let fresh air circulate throughout your home and invest in a quality ventilation system if needed.

Use Air Purifiers:

Consider investing in an air purifier with a HEPA filter to remove airborne particles such as dust, pollen, and pet dander. Place them in commonly used areas like the living room and bedroom for optimal effectiveness.

Avoid Synthetic Fragrances:

Many air fresheners and scented candles contain harmful chemicals that can pollute indoor air. Opt for fragrance-free or naturally scented alternatives to keep the air clean and fresh.

Clean Regularly:

Dust and vacuum your home regularly to reduce the buildup of allergens and pollutants. Pay special attention to carpets, upholstery, and other soft surfaces where dust mites tend to accumulate.

Minimize VOC Exposure:

Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are found in many household products like paints, varnishes, and adhesives. Choose low-VOC or VOC-free alternatives to minimize exposure and improve indoor air quality.

Maintain HVAC Systems:

Regularly change air filters and schedule routine maintenance for your heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems. This ensures optimal performance and prevents the circulation of pollutants.

Reduce Humidity Levels:

Excess moisture in the air can promote mold growth and worsen indoor air quality. Use a dehumidifier in damp areas like basements and bathrooms to maintain healthy humidity levels.

Choose Sustainable Materials:

When furnishing or renovating your home, opt for eco-friendly materials such as bamboo flooring, reclaimed wood furniture, and non-toxic paint. Not only are these options better for the environment, but they also contribute to better indoor air quality. By incorporating these simple practices into your daily routine, you can breathe easier and live more sustainably while enjoying a healthier indoor environment for you and your family. item.title: 7 Healthy Habits for Sustainable Living and Improved Indoor Air Quality
item.dc:creator: aaron@smbadvisors.com
item.content:encoded:
7 Healthy Habits for Sustainable Living and Improved Indoor Air Quality

Achieving a sustainable lifestyle isn't just about reducing waste and conserving energy; it's also about prioritizing your health and well-being. Here are seven healthy habits that promote sustainable living while improving indoor air quality:

  1. Cook from Scratch:

Embrace homemade meals made from fresh, whole ingredients instead of relying on processed foods. Not only is cooking from scratch healthier, but it also reduces packaging waste and minimizes exposure to preservatives and additives that can pollute indoor air.

  1. Practice Mindful Cleaning:

Take a mindful approach to cleaning by using eco-friendly products and minimizing waste. Choose reusable cloths and mops over disposable alternatives and opt for concentrated cleaning solutions to reduce packaging.

  1. Ditch Single-Use Plastics:

Reduce your reliance on single-use plastics by investing in reusable alternatives like stainless steel water bottles, glass food containers, and cloth grocery bags. By minimizing plastic waste, you're not only helping the environment but also improving indoor air quality by reducing the presence of plastic particles.

  1. Prioritize Outdoor Activities:

Spend time outdoors engaging in activities like walking, biking, or gardening. Not only does outdoor exercise improve physical and mental health, but it also reduces indoor air pollution by decreasing the time spent indoors.

  1. Practice Energy Efficiency:

Save energy and improve indoor air quality by optimizing your home's energy efficiency. Seal drafts, upgrade to energy-efficient appliances, and utilize natural lighting whenever possible to reduce reliance on artificial sources of light and heat.

  1. Support Local Farmers:

Choose locally sourced produce and other goods whenever possible to reduce carbon emissions associated with transportation. Supporting local farmers also promotes sustainable agriculture practices, which contribute to cleaner air and healthier ecosystems.

  1. Unplug and Disconnect:

Reduce electronic clutter and minimize exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMFs) by unplugging devices when not in use and limiting screen time. Create dedicated tech-free zones in your home where you can unwind and reconnect with nature.

Incorporating these healthy habits into your daily life not only benefits the planet but also enhances your overall well-being. By prioritizing sustainable living practices, you can enjoy cleaner air, better health, and a more fulfilling lifestyle.

item.title: Best Electric Only Builder
item.dc:creator: aaron@smbadvisors.com
item.content:encoded:
redT Homes Honored as Best Individual Electric Only Builder Overall in 2023 Xcel ESNH Program

redT Homes, a pioneering residential real estate development firm in Denver, is thrilled to announce its prestigious win of the 2023 Xcel Energy Sustainable New Housing (ESNH) Program Award for Best Individual Electric Only Builder Overall. This accolade underscores redT Homes' unwavering dedication to sustainable living and eco-conscious construction practices. The Xcel Energy Sustainable New Housing Program celebrates builders who excel in constructing energy-efficient homes that meet the highest standards of sustainability. redT Homes proudly meets the Xcel Energy evaluation criteria, ensuring that their homes are built with: - Tight construction that eliminates drafts. - Tight ducts that maintain proper air circulation without unexpected detours. - High-performance windows that block more heat and UV light than regular windows. - Properly installed insulation to guarantee comfort and quietness. - Energy-efficient HVAC systems that are appropriately sized to minimize energy waste. - Energy-efficient water heating systems to ensure an uninterrupted supply of hot water while conserving energy. - Energy-efficient lighting systems that illuminate homes without generating excess heat. - Independent inspection and testing confirming homes are at least 10 percent more efficient than the minimum energy standards for the state of Colorado. "Winning the Best Individual Electric Only Builder Overall award from Xcel Energy is a tremendous honor for redT Homes," said Vincent Deorio, CEO of redT Homes. "We are deeply committed to building homes that not only meet but exceed the highest standards of energy efficiency and sustainability. This recognition validates our efforts in creating healthier, more environmentally friendly living spaces for our community." redT Homes' dedication to sustainability goes beyond meeting the Xcel Energy evaluation criteria. They focus on constructing healthy homes from the ground up by ensuring they are also Zero Energy Ready, LEED Certified, Energy Star Certified, and EPA Indoor airPLUS Qualified. Furthermore, redT Homes delivers all-electric, solar-powered homes in Colorado, adhering to rigorous standards to minimize environmental impact and promote sustainable living. "We believe that sustainable living should be accessible to all," added Deorio. "By incorporating cutting-edge technology and sustainable building practices into every project, we are proud to contribute to Building A Greener Colorado and beyond." The recognition from the 2023 Xcel Energy Sustainable New Housing Program reaffirms redT Homes' position as a leader in the sustainable living space. With a commitment to innovation and excellence, redT Homes continues to set the standard for eco-friendly construction in Denver and beyond. For more information about redT Homes and their commitment to sustainability, visit redthomes.com.

About redT Homes

redT Homes is a residential real estate development firm based in Denver, Colorado. Committed to Building A Greener Colorado™, redT Homes offers a comprehensive suite of services, including land acquisition, entitlement, design, architecture, construction, and real estate-focused marketing and brokerage. With a focus on sustainability and innovation, redT Homes strives to create sustainably built, attainably priced homes across the metro area and beyond. Contact: Kevin Bree, VP of Brand Strategy

kevinb@redthomes.com

item.title: LEED Indoor Environmental Quality & EPA Indoor AirPlus
item.dc:creator: kevinb@redthomes.com
item.content:encoded:
LEED Indoor Environmental Quality & EPA Indoor AirPlus

  Creating healthy, comfortable, and sustainable indoor environments is more important than ever as we spend a substantial portion of our lives indoors. Indoor air quality and environmental factors directly affect our well-being, productivity, and long-term health. Recognizing this, organizations like the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) have developed standards like LEED Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ) and EPA's Indoor AirPLUS, both designed to elevate the quality and sustainability of indoor spaces. Together, these initiatives offer a comprehensive approach to indoor environmental quality, helping to minimize the impact of pollutants, optimize ventilation, and create healthier spaces. For building owners and developers, meeting these standards isn't just about certification—it's about fostering environments where people can thrive.  

What Is LEED Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ)?

LEED IEQ is a key component of the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) certification system, which aims to create healthier, more comfortable indoor environments. Within the LEED framework, "credits" are specific standards or strategies a building can implement to earn points toward certification. Each credit addresses a particular aspect of sustainability or occupant well-being, allowing buildings to accrue points by meeting these individual requirements. IEQ covers several credits within LEED, each targeting factors that impact indoor quality. These credits include areas like ventilation performance, which helps reduce indoor pollutants; low-emitting materials, which minimize harmful chemicals; and daylighting strategies, which introduce natural light to create a more comfortable indoor experience. By implementing these credits, buildings reduce their environmental footprint while prioritizing occupant health. IEQ also intersects with other LEED categories, such as Energy and Atmosphere and Materials and Resources, highlighting LEED's integrated approach. For example, efficient ventilation complements energy efficiency by optimizing HVAC systems, and sustainable materials contribute to better air quality by reducing pollutant levels indoors. Together, these interconnected categories create buildings that are environmentally responsible and support a healthy, comfortable, and sustainable indoor experience.  

Key Components Of LEED Indoor Environmental Quality

LEED IEQ emphasizes multiple components that address essential aspects of building design and operation. The following are the primary components within the IEQ category, each contributing to a balanced, sustainable environment where occupants can feel comfortable and thrive.

Ventilation And Airflow Management

Proper ventilation helps dilute indoor pollutants and maintain a steady supply of fresh air, which is vital for creating a healthier indoor environment. LEED emphasizes ventilation standards, such as those set by the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating, and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), which outline optimal airflow rates that balance indoor air quality with energy efficiency. Effective airflow management involves designing HVAC systems that ensure even distribution and prevent stagnation of air in specific areas. This includes the use of high-efficiency filters, balanced airflow, and strategic placement of vents to maximize air exchange throughout the space. By prioritizing ventilation and airflow management, buildings can reduce pollutants, allergens, and moisture levels, promoting a cleaner, more comfortable environment for occupants.

Low-Emitting Materials

Low-emitting materials are products designed to release minimal volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and other pollutants, reducing indoor air contaminants. In LEED-certified buildings, low-emitting materials play a crucial role in minimizing exposure to harmful chemicals that can impact occupant health, particularly respiratory health. Using materials that emit fewer pollutants, buildings contribute to better air quality, improving comfort and reducing potential health risks for those indoors. Examples of common low-emitting materials in LEED projects include:
  • Adhesives and sealants: Low-VOC adhesives and sealants are essential for minimizing off-gassing, which often occurs with conventional products used during construction and renovation.
  • Paints and coatings: Many LEED-certified buildings use low-VOC or zero-VOC paints and coatings, reducing the release of harmful chemicals that contribute to poor indoor air quality.
  • Flooring and carpets: Low-emitting flooring materials, including certain carpets and tiles, help maintain healthier indoor air by minimizing chemical emissions.
  • Furniture and furnishings: Low-emission furniture and furnishings are specifically manufactured to limit the release of formaldehyde and other harmful chemicals often found in synthetic materials and finishes.

Indoor Pollutant Control

Effective pollutant control strategies address both the sources of pollutants and their pathways, reducing the spread of contaminants within indoor spaces. This involves a combination of design practices, filtration systems, and regular maintenance to minimize the presence of allergens, chemicals, and particulates in the air. Key strategies for indoor pollutant control include:
  • Entryway systems: Installing mats and grates at building entrances helps capture dirt, dust, and other pollutants from shoes, reducing the contaminants brought indoors.
  • Enhanced filtration: High-efficiency filters in HVAC systems can capture airborne particles and pollutants, improving air quality by removing allergens, dust, and microbial contaminants.
  • Source control: Choosing building materials, furnishings, and finishes that emit fewer pollutants reduces the initial load of contaminants within the building.
  • Isolation of high-pollutant areas: Areas prone to higher pollutant levels, such as janitorial closets or printing rooms, are often isolated with separate ventilation systems to prevent pollutants from spreading to common areas.

Daylighting And Views

By bringing more natural light into a building, daylighting reduces the reliance on artificial lighting and creates a pleasant and productive environment for occupants. Exposure to natural light has also been shown to improve mood, support circadian rhythms, and improve overall well-being, making it a valuable element in sustainable building design. LEED-certified buildings use strategies like large windows, skylights, and strategically placed glazing to optimize daylight penetration throughout interior spaces. These buildings often incorporate open floor plans and low partitions, allowing light to flow more freely within shared areas. To further enhance the indoor experience, LEED promotes providing outdoor views from workstations and other frequently used spaces, giving occupants a visual connection to nature that can reduce stress and improve satisfaction.  

How Do These Standards Apply?

LEED standards for indoor environmental quality are crafted to enhance the health and comfort of occupants across various building types, from residential homes to large commercial spaces. Each standard is tailored to address the unique challenges and requirements of different settings. For example, residential buildings often emphasize low-emitting materials and ventilation to ensure a safe living environment. Commercial spaces prioritize efficient air filtration and moisture control to accommodate higher occupancy and activity levels. By implementing these standards, buildings can create indoor environments that meet rigorous sustainability goals and improve occupant satisfaction and well-being. To ensure a comprehensive approach to indoor environmental quality, LEED standards focus on the following interconnected strategies:

Indoor Air Quality Assessment

LEED's IAQ Assessment includes two key methods for ensuring air quality: a building flush-out and air testing, each with defined thresholds to confirm indoor air safety.
  1. Building flush-out: This approach involves systematically replacing indoor air with outdoor air to eliminate pollutants introduced during construction. LEED requires a total air volume of 14,000 cubic feet per square foot of floor area to be supplied before occupancy. If the building must be occupied before completing the full flush-out, LEED allows a partial flush-out of 3,500 cubic feet per square foot, followed by continuous ventilation until the total required air volume is met.
  2. Air testing: Alternatively, buildings may conduct air testing to verify that pollutant concentrations are within acceptable LEED-defined thresholds. This testing, conducted post-construction and pre-occupancy, assesses pollutants with specific limits as follows:
  • Formaldehyde: Must be below 27 parts per billion (ppb)
  • Particulate matter (PM10): Should not exceed 50 micrograms per cubic meter
  • Total volatile organic compounds (TVOCs): Should be below 500 micrograms per cubic meter
  • Carbon monoxide (CO): Must not exceed 9 parts per million (ppm), with no greater than 2 ppm above outdoor levels
For compliance, air testing results must meet these limits to ensure safe, high-quality indoor air. By utilizing these assessment strategies, LEED-certified buildings commit to high indoor air quality standards, enhancing occupant health, comfort, and well-being.

Controlling Indoor Pollutants

LEED emphasizes several effective strategies to control and reduce indoor pollutants, promoting healthier indoor environments. By managing pollutant sources and using non-toxic materials, LEED-certified buildings maintain cleaner air, contributing to overall occupant comfort and well-being. Key strategies include:
  • Use of low-emitting, non-toxic materials: As mentioned before, LEED encourages the use of materials and finishes with low or zero VOCs, such as low-VOC paints, adhesives, sealants, and flooring. These materials limit the release of harmful chemicals into the indoor environment.
  • Source control for high-pollutant areas: To prevent contaminants from spreading, areas with high pollutant potential—such as janitorial closets, garages, or print rooms—are often isolated from general areas. These spaces are equipped with separate ventilation systems, keeping pollutants contained and improving air quality in common areas.
  • Entryway systems: LEED promotes the use of entryway mats or grates to prevent dirt, dust, and other particles from being tracked inside by footwear. 
  • Enhanced filtration systems: High-efficiency filters, such as those with a Minimum Efficiency Reporting Value (MERV) rating of 13 or higher, capture particulates and other airborne contaminants. This is particularly effective in areas with high traffic, or in urban environments with elevated outdoor pollution.
  • Ventilation management: LEED-certified buildings are designed with ventilation systems that introduce fresh outdoor air while minimizing the recirculation of indoor pollutants. By meeting ASHRAE standards for ventilation rates, LEED helps ensure consistent air exchange, which dilutes indoor pollutants.
By implementing these pollutant control strategies, LEED-certified buildings create safer, cleaner indoor environments that prioritize the health and comfort of occupants, reinforcing the holistic approach to sustainable building design.

Improving Ventilation And Filtration Systems

LEED strongly emphasizes enhanced ventilation and filtration systems to support healthy indoor environments, recognizing that adequate airflow and high-quality filtration are essential for minimizing indoor pollutants and maintaining optimal air quality. Key strategies for improving ventilation and filtration include:
  • Enhanced ventilation rates: LEED encourages meeting or exceeding ASHRAE 62.1 standards for ventilation, which dictate optimal airflow rates for different building types and occupancy levels. By maintaining these standards, LEED-certified buildings ensure a consistent supply of outdoor air, reducing the buildup of pollutants indoors.
  • Demand-controlled ventilation (DCV): LEED promotes the use of DCV systems, which adjust ventilation based on real-time occupancy and CO₂ levels. By increasing ventilation in response to higher occupancy, DCV systems help maintain air quality during peak usage while reducing energy consumption when fewer occupants are present.
  • High-efficiency filtration: LEED recommends high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) or MERV 13 filters or higher to capture airborne particles, allergens, and pollutants. 
  • Outdoor air intake and exhaust: Properly designed ventilation systems in LEED-certified buildings include adequate outdoor air intake and exhaust systems to maintain airflow balance and ensure pollutants are effectively removed from indoor spaces. This also helps manage moisture levels, reducing conditions that can contribute to mold growth.
  • Regular maintenance of HVAC Systems: LEED underscores the importance of maintaining HVAC systems to prevent the buildup of dust and contaminants within them. Regular cleaning and timely filter replacement ensure that ventilation and filtration systems operate efficiently over time.
By prioritizing these advanced ventilation and filtration strategies, LEED-certified buildings provide a healthier indoor environment that meets sustainability goals and supports occupant well-being and comfort.  

The Intersection Between LEED And EPA Indoor AirPlus Program

The EPA's Indoor AirPLUS program is designed to ensure healthier indoor environments by reducing exposure to common indoor pollutants, improving ventilation, and addressing moisture control in homes. Created as an add-on to the ENERGY STAR® for Homes certification, Indoor AirPLUS establishes guidelines for home builders to exceed standard indoor air quality practices, providing healthier spaces for occupants. Indoor AirPLUS complements LEED IEQ by aligning with similar goals to enhance indoor air quality through strategies that minimize contaminants, improve ventilation, and manage moisture. While LEED IEQ focuses broadly on a variety of building types, Indoor AirPLUS is particularly targeted toward residential buildings. This program includes requirements for moisture-resistant materials, radon-resistant construction, and low-emitting materials, all of which align closely with LEED's pollutant control and ventilation standards.  Together, LEED IEQ and Indoor AirPLUS provide a comprehensive framework for creating healthy, comfortable indoor environments that prioritize occupant well-being and sustainability.  

Benefits Of LEED IEQ And EPA Indoor AirPlus Certification

Obtaining certifications like LEED IEQ and EPA Indoor AirPLUS provides significant benefits for building occupants, property owners, and the environment. By meeting rigorous standards for indoor air quality, ventilation, and pollutant control, these certifications ensure a healthier indoor environment, enhanced air quality, and a reduced ecological footprint. These advantages make certified buildings more appealing to both occupants and investors, aligning with modern expectations for sustainable and health-conscious spaces.

Health Benefits For Occupants

Arguably the primary benefit of LEED IEQ and EPA Indoor AirPLUS certification is the direct impact on occupant health. Certified buildings maintain strict standards for air quality, reducing the presence of pollutants like VOCs, formaldehyde, and particulate matter. Health benefits include:
  • Reduced respiratory irritation: Certified buildings help lower exposure to irritants by using low-emitting materials and enhanced ventilation systems, reducing respiratory issues and allergic reactions.
  • Improved cognitive function: Proper ventilation and CO₂ control have been shown to improve cognitive performance and alertness, which can be especially beneficial in work and learning environments.
  • Minimized risk of illness: Effective pollutant control and humidity management help reduce the presence of mold, allergens, and other contaminants that can contribute to chronic respiratory conditions or immune system stress.

Environmental And Energy Efficiency Gains

LEED IEQ and Indoor AirPLUS certifications also deliver environmental and energy efficiency benefits that contribute to a building's overall sustainability. Key advantages include:
  • Reduced environmental impact: These certifications help lower a building's environmental footprint by encouraging the use of sustainable, non-toxic materials and efficient ventilation systems. They also reduce the release of pollutants and VOCs.
  • Optimized energy use: Both certifications prioritize energy-efficient ventilation systems, such as demand-controlled ventilation (DCV) and high-efficiency filters, which maintain air quality without excessive energy consumption.
  • Enhanced market value and sustainability profile: Properties with LEED IEQ and Indoor AirPLUS certifications often experience higher market value and a reputation for sustainability, appealing to eco-conscious investors and occupants.
By prioritizing health, sustainability, and energy efficiency, LEED IEQ and EPA Indoor AirPLUS certifications create spaces that support both environmental responsibility and occupant well-being, providing long-term value and adaptability in an increasingly eco-focused market.  

How redT Homes Support LEED Indoor Environmental Quality Standards

At redT Homes, we are dedicated to integrating LEED IEQ standards across all facets of our services, ensuring that each project meets or exceeds LEED Gold certification. Our comprehensive approach spans design, architecture, and construction, all aimed at creating healthier, more sustainable living environments. Our in-house architecture team meticulously designs homes with a focus on sustainability and occupant well-being. We reduce indoor pollutants by selecting low-emitting materials and incorporating enhanced ventilation systems, aligning with LEED IEQ criteria. Additionally, our designs maximize natural light and outdoor views, promoting a strong connection to nature and enhancing indoor environmental quality. During construction, we implement rigorous quality control measures to maintain high indoor air quality. This includes protecting ventilation systems from contamination and conducting thorough air quality assessments before occupancy. Our commitment to sustainable building practices ensures that each home not only meets LEED standards but also provides a healthy living space for our clients. By seamlessly integrating LEED IEQ standards into every stage of our projects, redT Homes delivers residences that are both environmentally responsible and supportive of occupant health and comfort.  

Implement LEED IEQ In Your Building Projects For Sustainability

Incorporating LEED IEQ standards into building projects is essential for fostering healthier, more sustainable indoor environments. Practical steps to achieve LEED IEQ certification include focusing on enhanced ventilation, using low-emitting and non-toxic materials, controlling indoor pollutants, and maximizing natural light. The benefits of implementing LEED IEQ standards extend beyond health. These practices support sustainability by reducing a building's environmental footprint and enhancing energy efficiency through strategies like demand-controlled ventilation and high-efficiency filters. Over time, the commitment to LEED IEQ leads to long-term cost savings, as improved air quality and efficient systems reduce the need for repairs and health-related expenses. By following LEED IEQ guidelines, you can create spaces that prioritize occupant well-being, contribute to environmental goals, and offer valuable financial benefits through sustainable, resilient design. Learn how redT Homes can help you implement LEED IEQ standards and build healthier, sustainable homes.
